text.p: Andre Agassi, booed off court after a dismal performance at the ATP Tour championship on Wednesday, has been fined a hefty $50,000 for failing to appear at two pre-event functions.
Agassi, who said he had been suffering from a stomach upset and cold, was the only absentee among the world's top eight players at Monday's draw and press conference.

ATP officials said on Thursday that Agassi, who has pulled out of the rest of the tournament because of the illness, had been fined five percent of his Tour prize money for the year which totals around $1 million.
"It is a hard and fast rule," ATP Tour spokesman Peter Alfano said. "All the players must attend the media conference and draw. He has the right to appeal."
Agassi was booed, whistled and jeered after his straight sets defeat by world number one Pete Sampras in his opening match at the prestigious season-ending trournament.

The 12,000 German crowd, who paid between 180 and 230 marks ($120 and $153) for tickets, was clearly unhappy that Agassi had given such a poor display. Several hours later the American announced he was withdrawing from the event.
While Agassi still has a great deal of popularity among fans, the fine was the latest in a long list of altercations that the Las Vegas player has had with tennis authorities in recent years.

While he can produce brilliant tennis on his day, Agassi has at times disappointed tournament organisers and followers by pulling out of events very late, putting up lacklustre performances or simply refusing to play.
In 1993, Agassi was banned from a Davis Cup tie for failing to play a "dead" rubber against the Bahamas. Two years later he was fined for a late withdrawal from the Hong Kong Open.
His image in Germany was not enhanced last year when he made a tasteless reference to a knife at the German Open in Hamburg on the same court where Monica Seles was stabbed by a deranged fan.
The incident started when a spectator, disappointed by Agassi's performance, shouted "what a waste of money" at the end of the match.
The American was fined for unsportsmanlike conduct after he started shouting abuse at the fan and suggested that he might chase the player with a knife.

The ATP Tour was unable to explain exactly why it had fined Agassi despite his claimed illness. Alfano simply pointed to the organisation's rules which state clearly that a player will be fined five percent of his earnings if he fails to appear at the conference.
A statement said Agassi had been examined by the
tournament doctor on Thursday and had symptoms of a virus.
